subject: Grade 10 History
title: Grade 10 History class test (40 marks)
task: Answer all four questions in full sentences. Question 4 is a paragraph of about eight lines.

parts.question: In which year was the Bastille stormed?
Name the three estates of pre-revolutionary France.
parts.answer: The clergy, the nobility and the commoners (Third Estate).

parts.question: What was the slogan of the Revolution?
Give two causes of the French Revolution.
parts.answer: Any two: debt and bankruptcy, unfair taxes on the Third Estate, food shortages and the price of bread, Enlightenment ideas, the privileges of the first two estates.

parts.question: Explain the triangular trade.
parts.answer: Ships sailed from Europe with goods to Africa, carried enslaved Africans to the Americas, and took raw materials back to Europe.

parts.question: What was the Middle Passage?
parts.answer: The voyage across the Atlantic that carried enslaved Africans to the Americas.

parts.question: Name one person who campaigned to abolish the slave trade.
parts.answer: Any one: William Wilberforce, Olaudah Equiano, Thomas Clarkson.

parts.question: Give two effects of the slave trade on Africa.
parts.answer: Any two: loss of young people and labour, wars and raids between groups, damage to local economies, families and communities torn apart.

criteria.name: Question 3: The Cape under the VOC

parts.question: In which year did the VOC set up a station at the Cape?
Why did the VOC set up the station?
parts.answer: To supply fresh food and water to its ships sailing to and from the East.

parts.question: Give two consequences of Dutch settlement for the Khoikhoi.
parts.answer: Any two: loss of land, loss of cattle, smallpox and other diseases, being forced into labour as servants.

parts.question: In which year was slavery abolished at the Cape?
Write a paragraph explaining how the ideas of the French Revolution spread beyond France.
parts.answer: Any four, 2 marks each: Napoleon's wars and conquests; the ideas of rights and the Enlightenment; the Haitian slave revolt under Toussaint L'Ouverture; nationalism, constitutions and democracy in other countries; pamphlets, newspapers and print.
